important.name: pr_body markers match inline mentions, so prose quoting them is overwritten
important.summary:
_span (pr_body.py:40-49) finds BLOCK_START and BLOCK_END by bare substring count/find anywhere in the body. A PR description that mentions the markers in prose, as this feature's own docs do on one line (docs/RELEASES/v1.1.0.md:41 and skills/pr-sum/SKILL.md:81: between `<!-- pr-sum:start -->` and `<!-- pr-sum:end -->`), is read as holding a block: the first publish replaces the text between the two mentions with the summary, mid-sentence, breaking the module contract that text outside the markers stays as written. A body that mentions only one marker is refused instead of gaining a block. The same holds for the summary itself: a drafted summary or description that quotes a marker is published unchecked, so the next publish finds two starts and refuses. Neither publish_saved nor merge_block checks the summary for the marker strings.

Also (roast): merge_block wraps the rendered summary in BLOCK_START/BLOCK_END without checking whether the summary already contains either marker string. The summary of any PR that touches this feature will plausibly quote them. This PR's own release note and README both do, and a level 1 description of pr_body.py would too. The first `--gh` build then posts a body holding 2 start and 2 end markers. Nothing refuses it, because only the incoming body goes through `_span`. Every later build hits `_span` with starts=2, ends=2 and raises BodyError, telling the developer to fix the body by hand, when the text it chokes on is text `build` wrote. Inside the block a bare marker outside backticks also opens an HTML comment that hides the rest of the rendered block. In short, the first publish of a self-describing PR succeeds and every rerun after it fails.

Also (adv_code): merge_block wraps the summary between BLOCK_START and BLOCK_END without checking that the summary itself is free of those strings. A summary (or a Files Changed description) that quotes `<!-- pr-sum:start -->` or `<!-- pr-sum:end -->` (natural for any PR touching pr_body or the skill docs, including this one) is published once, leaving a body with two start and two end markers; every later build with gh then fails in _span with 'holds 2 start and 2 end pr-sum markers', and the advice to fix the body by hand cannot hold because the next publish writes the markers back.

Attack: summary = "# PR #339: x\n\n## Summary\n\nThe block sits between `<!-- pr-sum:start -->` and `<!-- pr-sum:end -->`.\n"; first, _ = merge_block("Hand text.", summary) succeeds and returns a body with first.count(BLOCK_START) == 2; merge_block(first, summary) then raises BodyError('the PR body holds 2 start and 2 end pr-sum markers, not one pair in order; ...'). Reproduced by probes/stdin_newlines.py in the run directory. End to end: capture --gh, draft a summary quoting the marker, build twice; the second build exits 1.
fix: Match the markers only as whole lines: count and locate them with re.compile(r'^<!-- pr-sum:start -->$', re.M) (and the end twin) in _span, since _block always writes each marker on its own line; add a test with a body that quotes both markers inline in backticks.
In merge_block, raise BodyError when the summary text itself holds a full-line marker, so a published block can always be found again.

In merge_block, raise BodyError when `summary` contains BLOCK_START or BLOCK_END. In run_build, check this before the .md is written when gh is stored: add a build problem in build_problems/run_build so nothing is published half-way. Add a test_pr_body case with a summary quoting both markers.

Neutralise the markers inside the summary before `_block` wraps it, for example by swapping `<!--` for a zero-width-joined or entity-escaped form that renders the same inside code spans. Then pin with a test that publish twice in a row on such a summary returns 'already holds this summary'.
In merge_block, raise BodyError when `summary` contains BLOCK_START or BLOCK_END, before touching the body, and add a test for it.
Or add a draft_problems check (pr_summary.py) that rejects the marker strings in the draft prose when gh is stored, so build fails before writing anything.

important.name: New --gh redirect note contradicts the receipt-only reply rule
important.summary:
SKILL.md:85-88 (added) tells the agent, when guidance asks for the summary on the PR, to build without the flag and then end the reply by telling the developer that rerunning with `--gh` puts the summary in the PR description. Step 4 at SKILL.md:339 still says `Output the receipt verbatim — nothing else.` The two rules now conflict on exactly the path B4 targets: an agent that honors line 339 drops the redirect (the judged act SC-1/SC-2 expect present), and one that honors line 88 breaks the receipt-only contract. The R-2 green run passed only because the scenario stops before build, so the receipt rule never came into play.

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md:85-88 (new) tells the agent, when building without --gh, to end the reply by telling the developer that rerunning with --gh puts the summary in the PR description. SKILL.md:339 still says 'Output the receipt verbatim - nothing else', and the skill's forked agent harness:messenger replies with 'The skill's receipt or output contract, verbatim, and nothing else' (plugins/harness/agents/messenger.md:98). The two rules cannot both hold, so the agent either drops the new hint or breaks the receipt contract. The trigger is also unclear: the paragraph can be read as 'always add the hint without --gh' or 'only when the guidance asked for the PR description'.

Also (roast): Step 1 (SKILL.md:85-88) tells the agent to build without `--gh` and then end the reply by telling the developer that rerunning with `--gh` puts the summary in the PR description. This is frozen behavior B4, judged 'present' in R-2. Step 4 (SKILL.md:339), unchanged by this PR, still says 'Output the receipt verbatim — nothing else.' An agent that obeys the last instruction it read drops the hint the spec froze, and the scenario that proved B4 never reached Step 4: it replied with commands and stopped.
fix: Amend SKILL.md:339 to carve out the exception, e.g. `Output the receipt verbatim, followed only by the --gh rerun note from Step 1 when the guidance asked for the summary on the PR.`
Or move the redirect into Step 4 next to the receipt rule, stated as the one line allowed after the receipt.

Amend SKILL.md:339 to 'Output the receipt verbatim, plus the one --gh line from Step 1 when it applies; nothing else', and limit the hint in SKILL.md:87-88 to runs whose guidance asked for the summary on the PR.
Or drop the reply-hint sentence at SKILL.md:87-88 and let pr_sum.py build print the hint as a receipt line (for example when the skeleton lacks gh), so the receipt-only contract stays intact.
Amend SKILL.md:339 to 'Output the receipt verbatim, followed only by the `--gh` note from Step 1 when the guidance asked for the summary on the PR.'

minor.name: On Windows the unchanged-block check never fires, so every build rewrites the PR body
minor.summary:
_gh passes the merged body through subprocess.run(text=True, input=...), which on Windows translates every LF to CRLF on stdin, so gh stores a CRLF body. merge_block always rebuilds the block with LF, so on the next build `merged == body` is False and publish issues another `gh pr edit` (an edit event on the PR) and reports 'block replaced' instead of 'already holds this summary', contradicting the module docstring's 'only when it changed'. The tests fake subprocess.run and never see the translation.

Attack: On win32: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'import sys; print(repr(sys.stdin.buffer.read()))'], input='a
b
', capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8') shows the child received b'a
b
' (the same call shape as pr_body._gh). Then body1, _ = merge_block('Hand text.', '# PR #7: x

## Summary

Adds a.
'); stored = body1.replace('
', '
'); merge_block(stored, same summary)[0] == stored is False, so publish edits again on every build. Reproduced by probes/stdin_newlines.py in the run directory.
fix: Send bytes: pass input=merged.encode('utf-8') without text=True for the edit call (decode stdout separately), so no newline translation happens.

Or compare after normalizing line endings: treat merged.replace('
', '
') == body.replace('
', '
') as unchanged.

minor.name: The fake gh drops cwd, so publish could ignore its repo argument and the tests would still pass
minor.summary:
pr_body._gh runs `subprocess.run([...], cwd=repo, ...)`, and that cwd is the only thing that picks the repository gh edits. `_Gh.__call__` records argv and `kwargs['input']` but never reads `kwargs['cwd']`, and every TestPublish test passes `tmp_path` without checking it. A regression that dropped `cwd=repo` would run gh in the process working directory and could edit a PR in another repository, and no test would fail.

Also (tests): test_a_body_over_the_github_limit_is_refused passes a 65536-character summary. The markers and newlines push the merged body about 40 characters past BODY_LIMIT, so changing `len(merged) > BODY_LIMIT` to `>=` (rejecting a body of exactly 65536 characters, which GitHub accepts) or to `> BODY_LIMIT + 1` would still pass.
fix: Record `kwargs.get('cwd')` in `_Gh.__call__` (for example `self.cwds.append(kwargs.get('cwd'))`) and assert `gh.cwds == [tmp_path, tmp_path]` in test_adds_the_block_with_one_read_and_one_edit.

Add a boundary case: let `room = 65_536 - len(START) - len(END) - 2`; assert `merge_block('', 'x' * room)` returns a 65536-character body, and assert `merge_block('', 'x' * (room + 1))` raises BodyError matching '65536'.

The docstring no longer describes how this module isolates gh.
fix: Extend line 6: '``gh`` is bypassed by constructing ``PrMeta`` directly and, for ``--gh`` builds, by replacing ``publish`` with a recorder (the gh calls of ``harness_lib.pr_body`` are tested in tests/lib/test_pr_body.py).'

minor.name: No test checks that a failed publish happens after the sentinel is cleared
minor.summary: run_build's docstring (pr_sum.py:337-338) says 'A successful build clears the PR's sentinel, before any publish', and the SKILL.md text at line 329 relies on a failed publish leaving a finished build. test_a_failed_publish_keeps_the_markdown checks the saved .md and the error text but never arms a --min-viz sentinel, so moving `min_viz_sentinel.clear` after `publish_saved` would leave a stale sentinel blocking Stop and still pass. No test covers auto_title together with gh either, so the order of the two receipt lines (retitle, then publish) is also untested.
fix: In test_a_failed_publish_keeps_the_markdown, arm the sentinel first (run a level-3 capture with --min-viz, or write it through min_viz_sentinel), then assert `not min_viz_sentinel.sentinel_path(active(), 1234).exists()` after the CaptureError.
Add a test that stubs both change_pr_title and publish, builds with auto_title=True and gh=True, and asserts the last two receipt lines are the retitle line followed by the publish line.

minor.name: The --gh consent rule has no contract test, unlike the --auto-title consent rule it mirrors
minor.summary: The file pins the --auto-title consent gate (line 41, the 'Never choose' line 42, the Common Mistakes row line 43) because it guards an outward write to the PR. This PR adds a second outward write, --gh, whose only guard against unasked use is skill prose: SKILL.md:79 ('`--gh` is the developer's consent to write the PR description'), SKILL.md:85-88 (guidance never adds the flag; build without it and tell the developer) and the Common Mistakes row at SKILL.md:368. The new tests at lines 31-36 check only that the argument hint names the flag, so an edit that drops or softens the consent text still passes. The module docstring (lines 1-5) also still scopes the contract to --auto-title alone.
fix: Add a test asserting `"`--gh` is the developer's consent to write the PR description" in _text()`, `"guidance never adds a flag" in _text()` and `"Adding `--gh`, or pasting the summary into the PR, unasked" in _section(_text(), "## Common Mistakes")`. Extend the 'Never choose' assertion on line 42 to include `, `--gh``, and widen the module docstring to cover the --gh consent and the level hint.
